html:
SMTO-CTX-0001 — The AI model said your request was too long for it

GUID: e8eba859-10fe-4596-a966-c9287f65109f
Slug: provider-context-length-rejected
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: context

What happened

  • The model server refused this step because it couldn't hold everything SMTO sent at once. The model didn't write an answer for this step; work the task finished earlier is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main model, then Limits and recovery. Clear Context ceiling so it says Auto, or set the server's real limit. Main is the model SMTO uses for most work; if its limit is set higher than the server allows, SMTO sends steps the server can't accept.
  2. In the same place, don't raise Output allowance to fix this. If it was raised a lot, lower it back. Room kept for the model's answer comes out of the same total, so a bigger allowance leaves less room for your material.
  3. Start a new task with a shorter request or fewer attached files. Model settings apply to new tasks, and a smaller request needs less room.

What success looks like

  • The new task gets past this step and the model replies without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the model server; the details include the server's own message. Don't change unrelated timeouts or limits to work around it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider rejected the inference request with an error matching context-length markers (for example "maximum context length" or "max_model_len"), classified as context_length_rejected.

What this means

  • The inference request reached the provider and was rejected with wording associated with context size. The category does not provide an exact token count or prove which input component caused it. Compare the served model capacity, requested input and reserved output; do not infer a tool-result delivery problem without those facts.

Why this can happen

  • Provider diagnostic markers identify a possible context-capacity rejection. The exact served limit and request measurements require confirmation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the saved model profile with the provider’s served capacity and tokenizer. Check input plus output reservation, including the provider’s chat template.

How to fix it

  • Compare the served model's real maximum length (for example vLLM --max-model-len) with the Context ceiling (context_window_tokens) and Output allowance (max_tokens) of the routed role in Settings › Setup › Model routing, align them, and run the work in a new task. The provider message carries no exact token count, so read the logged "Provider model request rejected" diagnostic before deciding which input caused it.
  • Check the served model’s context capacity against the saved inference profile. Increasing output tokens would reserve still more context.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Context Window: model-configuration / llm_context_window_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts the intact corrected request within its served context capacity.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Provider inference rejection matched context-limit markers. It is distinct from a local preflight rejection and does not identify which input component caused it.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-CTX-0002 — A step's results were too large to send to the model
  • SMTO-CTX-0003 — Your current request is too big for the model
  • SMTO-CTX-0004 — This step needs more room than the model has
  • SMTO-CTX-0005 — Your request and the model's answer won't fit together
  • SMTO-CTX-0006 — Your request is too large for SMTO to plan the task
  • SMTO-CTX-0007 — Provider tokenizer rejected context
  • SMTO-CTX-0008 — This task's saved model settings don't match the model
  • SMTO-LLM-0001 — Model request timed out
  • SMTO-EXE-0005 — A command ran too long and SMTO stopped it
  • SMTO-LLM-0037 — An older retry attempt ran out of time
